outcome: abdominal fat partitioning (subcutaneous, visceral, and hepatic fat)
cohort: 75 infants, categorized as appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA, n=40) or small-for-gestational-age (SGA, n=35 with spontaneous catch-up).
finding: Circulating exosomes decreased in size and increased in number from birth to age 7, with these changes influenced by fetal growth, and exosome size at age 7 correlating with liver fat.
birth_weight: Not explicitly mentioned, but study includes appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA) and small-for-gestational-age (SGA) infants.
